papers.title: Machian MOND: a variable $a_0$ in galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) generally resolves the need for dark matter in galaxy rotation curves introducing a single new constant of acceleration $a_0$. It is well known that increasing $a_0$ by a factor of a few can alleviate the residual mass discrepancies that MOND leaves in galaxy clusters. Within a parameter-free Machian interpretation of MOND motivated by $a_0\sim GM_u/R_u^2$ arising from the scalar sum of inverse-square distance gravitational mass contributions in the universe, we promote $a_0$ to a variable in spherically symmetric mass distributions, which is sensitive to mass external to the locally enclosed spherical region. Instead of a boost of $a_0$ in terms of gravitational potentials as in EMOND, we show that a boost in terms of this directionless inverse-square field roughly amounts to the boost needed to accommodate the mass discrepancies of MOND in galaxy clusters, while retaining MOND predictions in galaxies. We begin to generalize this approach by defining a new $a'_0=G\sum_{i}m_i/|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r_i}|^2-a_N$, where $a_N$ is the magnitude of the usual Newtonian acceleration.
